referents.category: addressee of a speech in dialogue

referents.why: Possessive second masculine singular on houses: Pharaoh's houses, Pharaoh being the addressee of the speech. Agrees in person, gender and number.
Possessive second masculine singular on officials: Pharaoh's officials, same speech and same addressee.
Possessive second masculine singular on people: Pharaoh's people, same speech and same addressee.
Third feminine plural. The only feminine plural candidate is frogs (w3), and the clause says they remain in the Nile, which is the frogs' stay. The masculine candidates are excluded by morphology.

links.why: The source named cl4 has no clause in this verse; it appears to be Exo.8.6#cl4, the purpose clause 'so that you may know'. That is not a narrated event the weqatal continues, and 'and then' is within-verse only by its own definition. The weqatal's link is to the command 'pray' (Exo.8.4#cl2), not to the purpose clause.

links.why: Pharaoh's command 'pray to the LORD' (Exo.8.4) followed by waw and a third-person weqatal saying what will come of it: the frogs will depart. cl0 opens with a separate waw, so this is the imperative-then-weqatal pattern, joined across the verse boundary by the full id.
